name: maybe_Actor_CreateNamedPartB
signature: void* Actor_CreateNamedPartB(void* actor, const char* name, u32 arg3)
summary: Allocates a 0xA4-byte actor part, copies the given name into it, runs the part constructor with the default 2D sprite/span parameter tables, then points its parent/offset fields at actor+0x74 and actor+0x84 and derives its mode fields from the scene mode byte at (work+8)->f_48+0x27F.
evidence: Only caller is Actor_CreateActionTable (0x0022AF9C), which registers the actor action/part factories, and the callees are Mem_AllocAligned_2 and std_memmove, so the allocate-copy-construct shape is confirmed; nothing distinguishes this 'B' variant from the A variant, so the name stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Action_CreateCut
summary: Action factory: takes a descriptor from Actor_Action_InitDescriptor and installs vtable 0x0075959C, whose +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10 slots are the three tiny overrides at 0x001BA290/0x001BA298/0x001BA294.
evidence: Caller Actor_CreateActionTable confirms it is a table-registered action factory, but neither the vtable nor its three override slots carries a name, so the 'Cut' action type is still only the N_040 proposal.

name: Field_SceneObject_SetSubObject
summary: Replaces the scene object's attached sub-object: detaches the current handle from the child list, stores the new one and inserts it. Used whenever a freshly created sprite or part is hung on an actor.
evidence: Four named callers (Field_CreateCollisionSprite, Actor_CreateActionTable, ActorAction_UpdateMoveTo, maybe_Actor_Action_CurveMove2_Update) all attach a newly created sprite/part, and the body is a pure detach/store/attach triple, so the operation is certain; the old 'Bc' suffix was a field-offset artifact (the body uses partSubObjectA), so it is dropped.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StartCut
summary: Start step of one field-action class: clears the target state, plays the action animation on the target actor through Gfx_Node_FaceObject, installs the completion callback at vtable+0x84 and shows the attach slots when the actor's +0x23C state is set.
evidence: No caller and no string; the three named callees (Gfx_Node_FaceObject, Model_AttachSlot_ShowAll, Os_GetGameWork) only confirm the start-animation flow, so the 'Cut' action type is still unproven.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StartDig
summary: Twin of 0x001BA2D8: same 120-byte clear-target/play-animation/install-callback flow, gating the attach-slot display on the actor's +0x238 state instead of +0x23C.
evidence: Same three named callees and the same 120-byte shape as 0x001BA2D8, differing only in the state offset and the callback label; no caller or string proves the 'Dig' action type.

name: maybe_Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdateMove
summary: Per-frame monster field-behaviour step. When the field is alerted it only re-aims the actor's effect part; otherwise it tracks the action slot, ramps turn rate and forward/strafe speed from the behaviour constants, runs Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdatePhysics and falls back to attract animation 1 once the actor has come to rest. Always returns 1, so the step never completes.
evidence: The body computes turnRate/moveSpeedScale/forwardSpeed/strafeSpeed and calls maybe_Monster_FieldBehaviour_UpdatePhysics, then selects attract animation 1 when the actor stops - that is movement, not an attack; the alerted branch only calls Gfx_EffectPart_SetDirection. 'Attack' was unsupported, so the verb is corrected to Move.

name: maybe_Field_Action_FinishCutIfDone
summary: Finish step: when the target actor reports its motion finished, switches it back to attract/idle animation 0. Byte-identical to 0x001BA46C, 0x0022AF34, 0x00302184, 0x003AE244 and 0x00477310 (template copies).
evidence: Only callees are func_00669DD4 and Actor_SelectAttractAnimation; no caller, vtable or string names the owning action class, so the 'Cut' label stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Action_FinishDigIfDone
summary: Finish step: when the target actor reports its motion finished, switches it back to attract/idle animation 0. Byte-identical to 0x001BA350.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x001BA350 (func_00669DD4 then Actor_SelectAttractAnimation(actor,0)); nothing supports the 'Dig' label.

name: maybe_Actor_FinishMotionIfDone
summary: Finish step on a controller whose actor sits at +0x28: when the actor reports its motion finished, switches it back to attract/idle animation 0. Same body as 0x001BA350.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x001BA350/0x00302184; the only difference is that the actor pointer comes from ctl+0x28, which does not identify the class.

name: maybe_Actor_Action_FinishLanding
summary: Finish step with selection 1: when the target actor reports its motion finished, switches it to attract animation 1, and always returns 1 so the step is reported complete.
evidence: Same template as 0x001BA350 but with argument 1 and a constant return 1; no caller or vtable names the action, so 'Landing' stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Action_FinishIfDoneEx
summary: Finish step: when the target actor reports its motion finished, switches it to attract/idle animation 0. Same body as 0x001BA350.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x001BA350/0x00300A44; the only caller is a field-action destructor, which does not identify the action class.

name: maybe_ActorAction_UpdateAttract
summary: Finish step on an action whose actor sits at +0x28: when the actor reports its motion finished, switches it to attract/idle animation 0. Same body as 0x001BA350.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x001BA350; no caller or vtable names the concrete class.

name: maybe_Ui_SpriteMarker_FinishAttract
summary: Finish step: when the target actor reports its motion finished, switches it to attract/idle animation 0. Same body as 0x001BA350.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x001BA350; the behaviour is certain but no caller or vtable supports the 'Ui_SpriteMarker' class label.

name: maybe_Field_ActorBehavior_SetAttractAnimation
summary: Finish step with selection 1: when the owner actor reports its motion finished, switches it to attract animation 1. Same body as 0x002C0628 minus the constant return.
evidence: func_00669DD4(ownerActor) then Actor_SelectAttractAnimation(ownerActor,1); no caller or vtable supports the 'Field_ActorBehavior' class label.

name: maybe_Ui_Message_PlayAttractAnim
summary: Finish step with selection 1 on the actor held at +0x28: when it reports its motion finished, switches it to attract animation 1.
evidence: func_00669DD4(animation) then Actor_SelectAttractAnimation(animation,1); the 'Ui_Message' class label is still unsupported by any caller or vtable.

name: Ui_ItemScreen_StepShowSelectionResult
summary: Item-screen step handler: once the page text scroll has finished it clears the context flags and chains to Ui_ItemScreen_ShowSelectionResult; otherwise it writes screen command 10, reactivates the screen and re-arms the next callbacks from g_uiItemScreenSelectCallbacks.
evidence: The named global g_uiItemScreenSelectCallbacks and the named callee Ui_ItemScreen_ShowSelectionResult pin the class to the item screen; the body's only real action is to wait for Ui_TextScroll_IsFinished and then show the selection result, so 'BeginSelect' is corrected to that verb.

name: Field_ApplyToActorsInRadius
signature: void Field_ApplyToActorsInRadius(void* scene, float* centre, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actor class list 4 and, for every actor inside the squared radius of the given centre (skipping state 2 when filter is 0), calls 0x005E7848(actor,2,0) and the actor's virtual +0x98.
evidence: Two named callers (Ui_SlideWindow_PlaySlideIn/PlaySlideOut) plus the walk over (work+8)->f_54 class list 4 with a squared-distance compare confirm it is the field-side radius iteration helper; what the per-actor callbacks do is still unknown, so the verb stays generic.

name: Field_DetachActorsInRadius
signature: void Field_DetachActorsInRadius(void* viewWork, float* centre, int filter)
summary: Walks the field actors, tests each against a squared radius and the state byte +0x26A, and detaches the matching ones through Field_AttachSlotObject while decrementing the view-entry counters at +0x15E0/+0x15E4.
evidence: Named caller Field_TalkCamera_ReleaseWork plus the named callees Field_AttachSlotObject/Field_UpdateDrawList and the two counter decrements confirm the detach-in-radius operation.

name: maybe_List_AddRowsFromArray
signature: void List_AddRowsFromArray(void* list, void* head, u32 heapTag)
summary: Converts the 0x20 embedded 0x1C-byte row descriptors at list+0x100 into fresh 0x18-byte list nodes, skipping rows whose +0x14 field is still 0x0FFFFFFF, and appends each node to the given list head.
evidence: The two named callers (Field_TalkCamera_ReleaseWork and Gfx_MeshObject_ApplySetupParams) belong to unrelated subsystems, so this is a shared row-list helper and the 'ViewWork' class label was wrong; the call-graph callee names (Snd_DetachChannel, Field_SlotOwner_Dtor) are themselves misnomers, so only the copy/append shape is used.

name: Ui_Widget_BindHpMpPane
summary: Lazily builds the 31-entry party-member table, then binds the win_hpmp1 pane to the widget's animation binding and sets its state from Party_CountAliveMembers (1 when at least one member is alive, 0 otherwise).
evidence: The named callees Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify with g_paneNameWinHpmp1 and Party_CountAliveMembers show the function is a pane bind plus an alive-count toggle, not a generic layout update; the body is a damaged decompilation (the else branch was dropped), so the name describes the visible effect only.

name: Ui_Widget_BindTalkPane
summary: Binds the win_talk pane to the widget's layout root through Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify and then resets that binding to state 0.
evidence: The body is a single pane bind against the named literal g_paneNameWinTalk followed by a state reset, so 'UpdateLayout' overstated it; the class is Ui_Widget because Ui_Widget_FindPaneAndNotify takes the widget as its first argument.

name: Ui_DiveStartWindow_SetupSlotAnims
summary: Lazily builds the party-member table, then picks one of two slot layouts from the save-work status flag and binds the corresponding animation refs and pane texts on the dive-start window.
evidence: The named caller Ui_DiveStartWindow_VariantCtor pins the class to the dive-start window, and the callees Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes/Ui_LayoutObject_Bind/Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText confirm the slot-animation setup.

name: Ui_PaneGroup_BindSlotAnimations
summary: For each of the 25 slots resolves the slot id, looks up its animation record and binds/resets the 0x14-byte anim ref at +0x48, then tail-calls the class update slot at vtable+0x14.
evidence: The named caller Ui_PaneGroup_BindPanes pins the class to the pane group, and the callees Ui_AnimRef_Bind/Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes confirm the per-slot animation binding.

name: Ui_CursorIcon_RebindWordAnims
signature: void Ui_CursorIcon_RebindWordAnims(void* self, void* layout, int paneIndex, u32 animSet)
summary: Rebinds the icon_cursor_word2/icon_cursor_word3 animations on the cursor icon, clears the word entries that are no longer active and then tail-calls the update slot at vtable+0x5C.
evidence: The string literals icon_cursor_word2/icon_cursor_word3 name the panes directly, which supports both the CursorIcon class and the word-animation verb; the body is a damaged decompilation (lost arguments), so only the visible effect is claimed.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyNameAnim
summary: Applies the resolved speaker name to the message window's name pane: plays the layout animation for the pane, measures the name string and shows only name-row entry 0 while clearing entries 1..10.
evidence: The only caller is the message-window talk-state advancer (0x00616900) and the callees are Str_WcsStr/Ui_Pane_PlayLayoutAnim/Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes, which fits a speaker-name pane update; the body is a damaged decompilation (unreachable blocks removed), so the name describes the visible effect.

name: maybe_Ui_ResetAnimRefAndInvalidate
summary: Resets the embedded animation ref at +0x174 and sets the dirty byte at +0x1C4 so the owner rebuilds its rows on the next update.
evidence: The body is Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes(&self->animRef,0) plus a dirty-flag write, so it does not reset a sub-widget; with no callers and no vtable sibling the owning class is unknown, so the name is corrected to what the body actually does.

name: Ui_TriplePane_SelectIndex
summary: Selects one of three 0x50-stride pane entries: enables and resets the animation ref at +0x70 of the entry whose index matches, and disables the other two.
evidence: The body loops exactly three times over 0x50-stride entries at +0x70, enabling the one whose index equals the argument and disabling the rest, so it is a three-way selector rather than a boolean SetActive.

name: Ui_Window_ToggleTwoPanes
summary: Stores the choice byte at +0x1DC and switches two mutually exclusive pane animation refs: the selected one is bound and enabled, the other is reset.
evidence: Both callers are slots of the same 0x0072B570 script-command table (0x0026343C and 0x00263744) and the body binds one of two mutually exclusive anim refs at +0x1E0/+0x230, which confirms the toggle.

name: Ui_Window_ReleaseLayoutAnims
summary: When the window owns its layout (+0x248), hides and releases the two layout animation refs at +0x9C and +0x27C. No memory is freed.
evidence: Four named callers on teardown/update paths (Ui_IconList_Tick, Ui_Delegate_BindActionB, maybe_Ui_IconList_UpdateState, maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_ApplyChange) and a body that only calls Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes on two refs show it releases animation refs, not layout spans.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_DtorB
summary: Deleting destructor of the guide window: stamps the vtable, releases the message object and the tween at +0x184, destroys the page list and frees the window.
evidence: The body is the standard release/destroy/free teardown and the matching constructor 0x00368AE0 is still maybe_, so the guide-window class link stays plausible but unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a large UI screen: stamps the vtable, releases the embedded layout refs and animation lists, destroys the 0x5C/0xFC/0x3B8/0x9C member arrays, tears down four embedded sub-objects and frees.
evidence: No caller and no vtable sibling; the body only shows the standard release/destroy/free teardown (Ui_LayoutRef_Release, std_destroy_range, Ui_Object_DtorBase), so the 'Screen' class label stays structural.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_DtorDeep
summary: Deleting destructor of a window-like object: stamps the vtable, releases the layout refs, destroys a 0x5C-stride array of 4 entries, destroys the embedded base at -0x1E0 and frees.
evidence: The teardown idiom (Ui_LayoutRef_Release, std_destroy_range 0x5C/4, Ui_Object_DtorBase, free) is verified but no named caller or vtable sibling identifies the class.

name: maybe_Ui_Screen_DtorDelete_2
summary: Deleting destructor of a large screen object: destroys a 0x9C-stride array of 0x23 entries, destroys the nested widget at -0x1684 and frees.
evidence: Only self-references; the layout and teardown order are consistent with a screen but no named constructor or vtable sibling confirms the class.

name: Ui_AnimObject_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor of the shared animation-object base: stamps vtable 0x0075A3E4, destroys the intrusive child ring and the embedded layout refs, and returns the enclosing pointer without freeing.
evidence: It stamps the same vtable 0x0075A3E4 as the deleting destructor 0x001D84CC, so it is that class's non-deleting twin; the five named callers (Menu_Senreki_QuestList_Init, Menu_Senreki_BuildListEntry, Ui_SenrekiMonsterList_SetupCamera, Ui_PresentPanel_UpdateEntryLayout, Ui_TimeWindow_Dtor) are all init/setup paths that reset an embedded object before reuse, which rules out the 'CursorIcon' label.

name: Ui_EmbeddedObject_ResetInPlace
summary: In-place reset of an embedded UI object: stores the new vtable/handler word at +0x18, destroys the pane at +0x64 and the list at +0x18, and returns the enclosing pointer.
evidence: Eight named callers across unrelated windows (Ui_TalkWindow_SetText, Ui_Message_SetArgsFromRecord, Ui_SmithMenu_StepOptionIndex, Ui_TxtLowerWindow_InitPanes, Ui_ThreeLineTwoSelectWindow_InitLayout, ...) all reset an embedded sub-object before re-initialising it, so this is a shared in-place reset rather than a member detach.

name: maybe_Ui_TitleWindow_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small window object: detaches the child sprite, removes the node from the owner ring, releases the tween/layout members and frees.
evidence: The teardown mechanism matches the other deleting destructors in this batch, but no named constructor or vtable sibling references a title window.

name: maybe_Ui_EquipWindow_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x00333240 for the same embedded equipment-window sub-object (identical body without the final free).
evidence: Same body as 0x00333240 minus the free, so it is a D0/D2 split; the owning equipment-window class is inferred only from the neighbouring panes.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x0036813C for the same embedded sub-object (same body without the free).
evidence: Same four-line body as 0x0036813C minus the free call, a deleting/non-deleting split; the class label is still first-pass inference.

name: maybe_Ui_IconText_Dtor
summary: Deleting destructor of a small embedded UI widget: stamps the vtable, releases the layout ref at +0x4C, runs the base destructor and frees.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_SakusenWindow_Dtor, which shows it is a member of that window but not that it is an icon-text widget; the body is the standard deleting-destructor template.

name: maybe_Ui_IconText_DtorBase
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x00383724: stamps the vtable, releases the layout ref at +0x4C and calls the UI base destructor.
evidence: Same body as 0x00383724 minus the free; no callers, so the class label stays unverified.

name: maybe_Ui_IconButton_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the single-icon button window: installs vtable 0x007699DC, releases the layout ref at +0x54, runs the base destructor and frees.
evidence: The vtable literal 0x007699DC is the only class evidence and its slot +0x20 (maybe_Ui_IconButton_InitPanes) is itself only 0.45, so the class stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_IconButton_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor twin of 0x003D2560: installs vtable 0x007699DC, releases the layout ref at +0x54 and tail-calls the UI base destructor.
evidence: Same vtable 0x007699DC; the class is only as certain as maybe_Ui_IconButton_InitPanes.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePage_DtorDelete2
summary: Deleting destructor of a large message-page object: stamps the class vtables, destroys the page at self+0x786 and releases a layout ref, but the readable body ends in halt_baddata with more than half of the teardown missing.
evidence: The readable C ends in halt_baddata() and depends on in_ZR/in_CY, so the body is a damaged decompilation and the class label cannot be raised above a guess.

name: Ui_AnimObject_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the shared animation-object base: installs vtable 0x0075A3E4, destroys the intrusive list at +0xB4, releases the two anim-ref lists and frees.
evidence: Vtable 0x0075A3E4 is shared with the non-deleting twin 0x001D8558, and the constructor that installs the same vtable builds exactly the two anim-ref lists released here, which confirms the class.

name: maybe_Ui_EmbeddedObject_Reset
summary: Resets an embedded UI object: stores the caller-supplied handler word at +0xB4, re-links the circular list head at +0xB8, copies a two-word descriptor and releases two layout refs.
evidence: The literal 0x00782F74 is a data descriptor rather than a vtable and the store lands at +0xB4, not +0x00; with no named callers the class stays unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_EmbeddedPanel_ResetTwo
summary: Resets an embedded two-reference panel: stores the parent at +0xBC, re-links the circular list head at +0xC0, copies a descriptor and releases two layout refs.
evidence: The two named callers (Battle_Hud_SelectMember, Ui_RankingPanel_Update) are unrelated, so this is a shared embedded-panel reset; the literal 0x00782FC4 is a data descriptor, so the class stays generic.

name: maybe_Ui_EmbeddedPanel_ResetOne
summary: Resets an embedded single-reference panel: stores the parent at +0x5C, re-links the circular list head at +0x60, copies a descriptor and releases one layout ref.
evidence: Same idiom as 0x003A57A0 with one reference; the literal 0x00782F88 is a data descriptor and there are no callers, so the class stays generic.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_Shutdown
summary: Two-stage teardown of an object that owns a thread handle, a critical section and a service object: closes the handles under SVC locks, releases the sub-objects and resets the vtable.
evidence: Vtable 0x0075A4DC slot +0x00 is this function and +0x04 is maybe_Svc_Object_Delete, but the class-specific slots are unnamed and several call-graph callee names here are themselves misnomers, so the owner stays unproven.

name: Ui_ListEntry_SyncSprite
summary: Refreshes one list entry's sprite: redraws sprite part f_11 by name in the normal path or hides it (mode 5) in the alternate path, then advances the list state machine for that entry id.
evidence: The named callees Ui_Sprite_DrawByName and Ui_GetCore plus the mode-5 hide path confirm the sprite refresh, and the state advance is a side effect of the same entry update.

name: Field_Actor_EndBehaviour
summary: Field actor behaviour end hook: flushes the owner through virtual +0x88 and, when actor->f_234 is set, triggers the field-2D visual update with flag 0 and resets the animation instance.
evidence: The only caller is Field_Action_StepEnd and the body flushes the owner then resets the anim instance, which is the behaviour-end hook; it is byte-identical to 0x001E1534, so one of the two names is approximate.

name: Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_ReleaseEntries
summary: Destroys the three 0x10-byte entries of a screen-view entry through std_destroy_range with element destructor 0x00295660, frees the block and clears the pointer and state bytes.
evidence: Two named callers (Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_Reset, Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_ResetShort) plus the matching builder 0x001E4A40 show it releases the screen-view entry's 3-element 0x10-byte array, so the 'Ui_SubTable' class label was wrong.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_StepConfirmSell
summary: Shop item-list step handler: once the text scroll has finished it masks the flags to the top byte and chains to Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry; otherwise it writes screen command 0x1E, reactivates the screen and re-arms the default callbacks.
evidence: The named callee Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry pins the class, and this is the only one of the twin step handlers that calls Shop_SellItem, so the step is the sell confirmation rather than the opaque command-id name 'Step1E'.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopItemList_Step1F
summary: Shop item-list step handler: on a finished text scroll it chains to Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry with confirm flag 0x10100; otherwise it writes screen command 0x1F, reactivates the screen and installs the default callbacks.
evidence: Mirror of 0x001E935C with command 0x1F and flag 0x10100 and the same named callees, but unlike its twin it calls no sell/buy helper, so which shop action it confirms is still unproven.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_HidePane
summary: Hides the shop list pane at self+0x244C: refreshes the pane, re-links it into the owner and broadcasts message 0 (hide/close) to its children.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_ShopItemList_ConfirmEntry and the body re-links the pane at self+0x244C and broadcasts flag 0 to its children, so it hides the shop list pane rather than detaching a child.

name: Ui_ItemScreen_HideSubPanel
summary: Resets the sub-panel node at +0x1D0, inserts it into the window's list at +0x110 and broadcasts flag 0 (hide/close) to its children.
evidence: Both named callers (Ui_ItemScreen_HandleInput, Ui_ItemScreen_ConfirmEntryEx) run it while closing the item page, and the body re-links the sub-panel at +0x1D0 and broadcasts flag 0 to its children, which pins both the class and the hide verb.

name: maybe_Item_GetRecipeMaterialAvailability
signature: void Item_GetRecipeMaterialAvailability(void* result, int materialIndex, int requiredAmount)
summary: Compares a required forge-material amount with three fields of its data-manager record and writes a 0..3 availability class plus the effective amount into the caller's result record.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList, which reads result bytes 0..3, and the body compares the required amount against three record fields and writes a 0..3 class plus the effective amount; the body is a damaged decompilation (halt_baddata), so the name stays a guess.

name: Save_SetMaxByte
summary: Copies the 11-byte save-work block at (work+0x24A98)+0x88ED to the stack, raises the byte at the given index to the value when the value is larger (0xFF always writes) and writes the block back.
evidence: Four named callers (Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList, Ui_RecipeBook_ClearVariantSelection, Ui_FiveRowStatusWindow_InitRows, Ui_SelectRowWindow_InitPanes) plus the base work+0x2D385 = save work+0x88ED confirm it is a max-write into the 11-byte save-work block.

name: Save_ClampMinByte
summary: Lowers the byte at (save work+0x88ED)+5+index to the value when the value is smaller and returns whether it changed; the block is written back only on change.
evidence: Same 11-byte block family as 0x001F3084 (base work+0x2D385) and two named callers (Ui_Window_AppendControlBytes, Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList); the body lowers the byte at +5+index and returns whether it changed, which matches the name.

name: FieldParty_ApplySlotAndLayoutBalloons
signature: void FieldParty_ApplySlotAndLayoutBalloons(void* group, int slot, int mode)
summary: Applies a formation slot through the group's vtable +0x40, resets the +0x54 state when the mode is 0, and when more than one of the 16 live-member slots at +0x1C is non-null re-runs Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons.
evidence: The two named callers (Battle_ActorAction_SetupFormationScale, FieldParty_Talk_Update) and the named callee Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons confirm the slot-apply plus balloon-relayout pair.

name: Actor_QueueEquipmentMessage
summary: Queries the actor's equipment vtable for the item in the given slot, maps it to a message id through Ui_LookupMapValueById and pushes a battle-style message entry for the actor.
evidence: The named callees Ui_LookupMapValueById and Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry confirm the item-to-message-id-to-queue flow, and the caller passes equipment slots 0x20/0x21/0x22.

name: Model_SyncAttachmentPose
summary: Per-frame model sync: when the model's type tag is 0x76/0x11B and it sits in the group's slot array, or its type is 0x79, it runs the attachment/pose update.
evidence: Twelve callers, all field/battle per-frame update loops (FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine, Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn, Field_ActorActionSeq_UpdateMain, Battle_Sequence_Update, ...), and the named callee Model_SetDirectionToTarget confirm a shared per-frame model pose sync; the type-tag gate 0x76/0x11B/0x79 is the only class evidence.

name: maybe_Menu_TalkParty_WaitPanels
summary: Polls the 24 embedded sub-panels at self+0x1C until all report done, then on a button press or timeout closes the field UI core and creates the map cursor when self+0x9C is set.
evidence: The 24-slot wait loop over self+0x1C virtual +0xC and the named callees Input_GetButtonState/Ui_GetCore/maybe_Ui_CreateMapCursor confirm the wait-then-close flow, but there are no callers and the TalkParty ownership comes only from the neighbouring function 0x002175BC.

name: maybe_Camera_FollowSelectNext
summary: Steps the follow-camera selection index in the candidate table at self->f_28->f_248, wrapping or clamping it by the direction byte at self+0x3C, notifies the owner through vtable +0x8C and returns whether the index changed.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Camera_FollowIndexUpdate, which calls it twice as a forward/backward step, so the camera class rests on an unproven caller name even though the stride-0x18 table and index clamp are visible.

name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_UpdateApproach
summary: Approach action update: picks an animation from the actor type/state, moves the actor forward with deceleration and switches to the attract animation when the timer expires.
evidence: The only caller is Field_Actor_PlayBreakEffect, which does not fit an approach action, and 'approach' is inferred purely from the motion maths; the named callee Actor_SelectAttractAnimation only confirms the idle fallback.

name: maybe_Model_SetChildAnimationName
summary: When the pending flag at self+0x52 is set, selects an animation name string from the child byte at +199 and passes it to the child model node's virtual +0x84, then clears the flag.
evidence: The body passes the literal 'Walk' (or a variant chosen by child byte +199) to the child model node at +0x28 through virtual +0x84 and clears the pending flag, so it sets an animation name rather than a 'name string variant'; with no callers and no named callees the class stays a guess.

name: GameWork_LazyInitAndCountRoster
summary: Lazily builds the 0x2FB28-byte 31-element work block on first use, then returns whether Spirit_CountRosterEntries on work+0x24A98 is below 50.
evidence: The body is the standard 0x00764B84 lazy construction of the 0x2FB28-byte 31-element block followed by Spirit_CountRosterEntries(*work+0x24A98) < 0x32, which matches the name; the call-graph callee names (Sound_Track_ApplyChannelKey, Text_BuildGlyphQuads) are misnomers.

name: maybe_Battle_Group_BuildFromString
summary: Resolves a party/battle member specification (type char plus index byte, with a special 'R' form) into an id, checking party size and the member's skills and offhand state.
evidence: The named caller Battle_BuildUsableSlotMask and the tail function maybe_Battle_Group_BuildFromString_Tail support the parse-and-resolve shape, but the decompilation is damaged, so the exact spec grammar stays a guess.

name: maybe_Battle_ApplyUnitHpChange
summary: Validates the acting unit's effect state and HP, queues action 0x553/0x554 and records it, or subtracts the action power from the unit and returns 1.
evidence: The named callees Battle_QueueActionEx and Battle_ActionRecord_GetPower confirm the queue-or-apply split, but the direction (damage versus heal) and the meaning of 0x553/0x554 remain open, and there is only one caller.

name: Battle_Ui_PushActionMessage
summary: When self+0x128E is set, pushes the action row's +0x154 message id for the owner, or the +0x152 id when self+0x128F is set.
evidence: The body only pushes one of two action-row message ids (+0x154 or +0x152) through Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry, and the named caller Battle_Ui_UpdateMessageSequence is a message-sequence step, so nothing supports the item-drop reading.

name: Field_Marker_UpdateScreenOffset
summary: Resolves the marker's 2D actor, applies the stored anchor offset (+0xD8 or the +0xE4 array entry) and writes the adjusted screen coordinates, then runs the overlap tests.
evidence: The named caller Field_CreateCollisionSprite plus the Field2D getters and Field_TestAreaOverlapA/B confirm the anchor-offset plus overlap-test flow.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_ReleaseRecords
summary: Releases an overlay's records: clears the entries at +0x2C, sets the scene node's +0x7D flag, returns 57 0x30-byte records through Gfx_Trail_PushSample and finishes with 0x00239A1C.
evidence: There is no caller; only the entry clear, the scene-node flag and the 57-record return loop are certain, so the class is not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_DtorDelete
summary: Deleting destructor: installs the class vtable, releases the entry objects at +0x2C, zeroes the count, runs the widget base destructor and frees the block.
evidence: The body ends in the widget base destructor and the free helper, so the deleting-destructor role is certain, but the class rests only on the neighbouring horse-race code.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_AttachNamedSpriteA
summary: Attaches a named sprite to a panel: clamps the record type byte +9, sets the sprite up with Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteA, builds the 0x16-byte pane name and creates the frame colour animator.
evidence: The named callees Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteA, Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh and Gfx_CreateFColAnimator confirm the attach-sprite flow, but there are no callers and the owner class is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_AttachNamedSpriteB
summary: Second named-sprite attach: identical to 0x004DD4A8 but uses Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteB before building the 0x16-byte pane name and the colour animator.
evidence: Same body as 0x004DD4A8 with Field_SpriteActor_SetupSpriteB; the owner identity and the absence of callers keep the maybe_.

name: maybe_Model_Actor_SendPoseGroupCommand
summary: Queries the actor state (virtual +0xE8 with 0xDA), resolves the actor through Menu_FindActorByHandle and sends a pose group from Battle_SelectPoseGroup through 0x005E7848.
evidence: The named callees Menu_FindActorByHandle and Battle_SelectPoseGroup confirm that a pose-group command is sent, but nothing supports the 'idle' reading or names the 0x2D-frame timer, and the body is a damaged decompilation (maybe_ fields, damaged poseCommand).

name: maybe_Fs_Request_WaitForService
summary: Invokes a service-object method and, on failure, formats the result into the request; otherwise it clears the request and spins waiting for the service reply.
evidence: The named callers Fs_Request_Build/Svc_AcClient_Cmd0004 and the named callees Svc_Object_InvokeAndStoreResult/Fs_FormatResultCode fit invoke-then-wait, but the wait loop decompiled to bad instruction data, so the body is a damaged decompilation.

name: Svc_ContentInfo_IsCacheCurrent
summary: Reads the 0xD0000 system word, fetches the content info under the global monitor and compares the stored halfword at +0x2C with the low half of the system word to decide whether the cached content is current.
evidence: The body reads the 0xD0000 system word, fetches content info under the global monitor and compares the stored halfword at +0x2C with the low half of the system word, and the callers are the icon-cache load/write paths (maybe_Ui_IconCache_BeginLoad/BeginWrite) plus Fs_BuildContentInfoArchivePath.

name: Svc_ContentObject_QuerySize
summary: Queries a 2-byte attribute through vtable+0x2C, creates and initialises a 0x36C0-byte content object, fetches the content info and returns 0 only when the cached size covers the queried value.
evidence: The body queries a 2-byte attribute through vtable+0x2C, creates the content object with Svc_ContentObject_CreateAndRegister, fetches content info and returns 0 only when the cached size covers the queried value; nothing reads a raw file, so the old Cecd_QueryRawFile wording was speculative.

name: Object_ReleaseOwnedMember
summary: Releases the owned sub-object pointer at self+0x18 when it is non-null and clears the field; a generic helper used by VRAM bank setup, container destructors and script destructors.
evidence: Five generic callers (Gfx_ShutdownGlobalManagers, Gfx_VramBank_Setup, Container_Value_Dtor, Container_Value_DtorB, maybe_Svc_Cecd_ResetMailbox) confirm a shared helper, and the body is a null-checked release of self+0x18 followed by a clear.

name: Regex_BuildSuccessorList
summary: Builds the value set for one regex expression node: allocates a memo entry, links it into the node, records the operand and visited links and recursively copies the operand values into the result list.
evidence: The named callers Regex_OpBuildOperandSets/Regex_OpBuildOperandSetsSingle call it per operand node and its result is a value set (Container_Value_Set), which confirms the successor/value-set build.

name: maybe_Sound_SubmitAdpcmFrame
summary: Packs one ADPCM frame for the DSP: splits eight sample bytes into sixteen nibbles, combines them with the channel's predictor/step values and writes the result, then waits for the DSP event.
evidence: The named caller Sound_SubmitAdpcmBlocks and the packing loop are readable, but the body is a damaged decompilation (unaff_r5, bad instruction data, a bogus func_0x005d1f7a target and an impossible Os_CreateThreadWithStack call), so the frame layout cannot be re-verified.

name: Gfx_ModelPart_ReleaseAll
summary: Releases every 0x3C-byte part record of a part list, freeing each part's GPU blocks through Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock while optionally keeping the caller's part, and drops the tracked resources.
evidence: The named callers Gfx_ModelSlot_Release/Gfx_ModelSlot_Replace/Fx_SpawnEmitter and the named callees Mem_FreeGraphicsBlock/Gfx_UnregisterResources confirm the release pass; the body is a damaged decompilation (unaff_r4), so only the pass itself is claimed.

name: Gfx_AllocGraphicsBlockByRegion
signature: u32 Gfx_AllocGraphicsBlockByRegion(u32 kind, u32 size, u32 force)
summary: Selects a graphics memory region by kind (1 -> the 0x20000 region, 2 -> the 0x30000 region), asks that region's allocator for a block and, when a block came back or force is set, submits the resulting memory write.
evidence: The named caller Gfx_ModelInstance_InitFromResource and the named callees Gfx_CmdQueue_SubmitEntry/Gfx_GpuCmd_EnqueueMemoryWrite confirm the region-select plus block-alloc plus command-submit flow.

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_BindPartyMember
summary: Virtual-slot initialiser that clears the slot ids, resolves the action row for self->f_1230 and, when it is valid, copies the ids and rebuilds the embedded FieldParty through FieldParty_InitFromParams and Battle_Actor_Init.
evidence: The named callees Game_GetDataManager, FieldParty_InitFromParams, Battle_Actor_Init and the action-row resolver 0x0063FD24 support the shape, but there are no callers at all, so the class stays a guess.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_ReleaseRowHandle
summary: Damaged decompilation: Ghidra stops at a bad instruction right after Os_GetGameWork, so only the caller set (the Field_Gimmick row and selection routines) is usable.
evidence: The body is halt_baddata() after Os_GetGameWork, so it is a damaged decompilation; all three callers are Field_Gimmick routines, so the class is right but the per-row release semantics are unverified.
